steps.name: Shrine Patrol
steps.text: Citizen, if you are here to view the Nativity, please queue up at the security check line in the plaza.

steps.name: Shrine Patrol
steps.text: You've been dawdling here for a while.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Oh, I'm sorry!

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I'm just waiting for someone...

steps.name: Shrine Patrol
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Shrine Patrol
steps.text: There is a large amount of traffic going in and out of the shrine today. We ask for your cooperation and to refrain from loitering.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: S-Sorry.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: El's been in there all day.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: The plan was to blow up important structural elements in the shrine to prevent the ceremony... whatever it's called... from being held as scheduled.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: She should have been out by now... don't tell me she's been caught?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: But I've been here all this time, and there's been no movement inside...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: But El must have ran into some kind of trouble that's holding her up...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Come on, Vani, think... what can you do?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I have two small Originium powder tubes that I could turn into an improvised bomb.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: It won't be very powerful, but it should cause enough commotion to distract the guards and allow El to...

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Let's set it here.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: No one's paying any attention... all I need to do is set it off—
Vannini's arm finds the barrel of a gun, preventing it from moving down any further.
Don't let that thing go boom, girl.
Stand up, slowly.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: R-Reverend Gun-knight...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Those tools and all, you work at a firearms workshop?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I have ten minutes. Explain yourself, girl.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: What are you up to here? Or should I say, who are you trying to cover for?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Let's go, El.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: What about Master Pag?

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Magister's sleeping. His vision's been getting worse, and the doctor wants him to get plenty of rest.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: We shouldn't wake him if we're careful.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: There's something I need to tell you first, Vani.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: It's so weird when you talk all serious like that...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Ahem. Listen—

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: If you get caught, just give me up to whoever it is, whether it's the Pontifica Cohors, the executors, or the gun-knights. Don't worry about me.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: I came in the middle of the night, kicked your door open, and forced you to make bombs and stand guard for me.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: You're an innocent little angel who doesn't know anything!

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Wha?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: That's my condition for letting you come with me.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: Just because I'm shy doesn't mean I'm a coward!

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Haha. I know. And I'm glad you decided to help me.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: The Curia seems to be taking that ceremony very seriously. Who knows what punishment they have in store for somebody trying to bomb it?

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Besides, Laterano is very different from how I remember it.

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: But...

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: No but's or what about's! I can handle this on my own.

steps.name: Exusiai
steps.text: Besides, Penguin Logistics company culture says, never share the glory when you can hoard it all for yourself!

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Vannini
steps.text: I-I came on my own.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Interesting girl.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Old men like me don't get a lot of chances to talk to the youth. Unfortunately, the ceremony is about to begin...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: If you won't talk, I'll have to hand you over to the executors of the Notarial Hall.
Stop right there, Patrizion!
Don't think I don't recognize that sanctimonious face of yours just because you're hiding it behind a hunk of sheet metal!

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: *pant* *pant* My... my legs...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Pag?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: What do you mean? Is something going on with the Holy City? Would you care to explain, or do I have to guess from your meaningful glances at one another?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This is not related to our investigation, Sister.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: At this time, I have not determined that you need to know more.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: In any case, Arturia, you'll have to come back with us.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I don't dislike you. In fact, I am rather fond of you. But if your actions will bring harm to Landen Monastery, then I-I'll pull no punches!

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: May I ask you something, Sister Hildegard?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You love the monastery and Laterano, don't you?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Or should I say—how did you establish an emotional connection to Laterano as a Liberi?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Well... I've lived at Landen Monastery for a long time. I was brought up by the brothers and sisters there, and we worked together to make bread and beer, doing our best to keep the monastery solvent.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I belong here. Of course I love this place.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: If you're asking why there are so many Liberis in the Holy City... you've read The Saints' Travels, haven't you?

spans.text: If you're asking why there are so many Liberis in the Holy City... you've read

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Don't tell me you only used it to make your paper dragonfly...?

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: According to The Saints' Travels, the first encounter between the Liberi and Laterano began with a herd of burdenbeasts.

spans.text: , the first encounter between the Liberi and Laterano began with a herd of burdenbeasts.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Many years ago, a group of Liberi were scattered by a herd of burdenbeasts while seeking water in the wilderness. The animals carried grain on their backs, forming an orderly procession as they traveled into the distance.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The Liberi spent great effort to hunt the burdenbeasts. They never imagined that these creatures of the wild could move in such orderly manner, so they followed the beasts.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Then, the Liberi saw the halo-bearers in the fields, singing as they guided the herd of burdenbeasts into the assembly of pearl-white buildings behind them.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: At a time when the Liberi still lived naked in the wild, seeking water and game, those people had learned to tame wild beasts, and build cities safe from Catastrophe.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: More importantly, the Liberi found that those people had a confidence and optimism that was alien to the Liberi.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Because of their halos, and 'empathy'...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Uh-huh.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: From the moment of their birth, they could feel each other's feelings and understand one another. They rarely knew conflict, and they were able to overcome crises that would destroy any other race.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: They created the perfect order, naming it the Law.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: I can understand that feeling.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Even as the Curia cut off funding to the monastery, even as its buildings fell into disrepair, even as I fretted over the monastery's books...

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: The Sanktas of Landen Monastery never seemed to fear that there might come a day when we would have to close our doors.

steps.name: Hildegard
steps.text: Their confidence and optimism let them accept the presence of the Liberi nearby, learning from them and becoming part of the whole.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Yes. Over the ages, the Sanktas have almost completely assimilated the Holy City's Liberi... other than the halo, which can never be shared.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We are too special, able to take in everything... like a concerto with a clear main theme.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Laterano has never been just a warm, cozy little cottage for the Sanktas, Fede.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: After you escaped, you went searching for a 'missing pregnant woman' from a nomadic abbey, but there have been no such recent reports of a missing person in Notarial Hall records.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Explain yourself, Arturia.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: A poor mother has gone missing in Laterano. A little incident that no one has paid any heed...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But, by chance, I had once touched the note of her heart while playing in the wheat fields—

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: And I discovered where she went.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Do you mean...?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Patience, Fede. Wait and see.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: We've come this far. You don't need me to explain it to you.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Is this the girl you took in?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: You'll have to forgive, Reverend Gun-knight, that I don't have the adoption papers on me.

spans.text: , that I don't have the adoption papers on me.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: What? If you can take in a Liberi, why can't I take in a Sankta?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: She's a good girl. You know, you are the only Sankta I've ever had a real problem understanding.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: That mouth of yours...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: How long has it been since we last met, Pag?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I forget. Never thought much about it. Didn't think I would need to.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Back on topic: Your apprentice just attempted to—

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: On my orders.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: An act of protest. Is that so hard to understand?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: The Curia shut down over a hundred firearms workshops overnight. My livelihood for decades, the shop I counted on for my retirement, all gone in the blink of an eye.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: When I heard you were throwing some party here, I thought I might force the Curia to hear the voice of this humble citizen, in front of all these honored guests.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I should have done it myself, but I'm old, and my legs and eyes aren't what they used to be, so I had the girl run this errand for me.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I thought you had gone into a different line of work, Pag.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Screw that.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Why should I? When you still have the nerve to use that gun I made after you exiled Gia from Laterano?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: I just gave up being a dedicated supplier for you gun-knights.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: True.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: And how exactly do you plan on dealing with this?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: We're caught red-handed attempting to bomb the Shrine of Nurtury and sabotage the Nativity.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Will you once again 'escort' your friend out of Laterano, as a gun-knight sworn to protect the sanctity of Paradise?

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: One who just happens to be a Liberi as well.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: This has nothing to do with you being Liberi, Pag. If you have indeed violated the Law, then I have no choice but to suffer another parting.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: And yet... I see that no harm was actually done, was there?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Take your apprentice and go.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Hmph.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: Come along, Vani.

steps.name: Paganini
steps.text: (Grab onto me. I left in a hurry and forgot the new glasses you got me.)

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Reverend, the man's story doesn't stand up to scrutiny.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: I know.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: The appropriate course of action would be to take them in for questioning and eliminate any potential risk...

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: That won't be necessary... besides, I don't need another fight with that old bloke.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: This bomb is simple, improvised. The girl obviously made it on the spot... which means that her accomplice is still inside.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Reassign an extra team of gun-knights and work with the patrols to ensure the shrine's security.

steps.name: Gun-Knight
steps.text: Yes, Reverend.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Strange. Is she still in the Shrine of Nurtury?

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Cardinal Aide Amos.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: R-Reverend Patrizion. L-Long time no see.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Long time indeed.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: What are you all worked up about?

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Have you seen Cardinal Lemuen? There's something I wanted to check with her.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: She hasn't returned to the Seventh Tribunal since visiting the Shrine of Nurtury.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: If this has something to do with the explosion, I must be kept in the loop.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: Yes, Reverend.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I bumped into a Sankta on Via Borgos in Pagus Faber to complete the takeover of a firearms workshop. There was a visible reaction from the Cardinal when I mentioned this to her.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: I checked the appearance of the individual I encountered against the database of registered citizens, and found a match in the external personnel files.

steps.name: Amos
steps.text: She must have been on the scene of the explosion in Pagus Stevonus. She has... certain ties to the Cardinal.

steps.name: Patrizion
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: ...I don't have much time, Sister. I must return to the Shrine of Nurtury.

steps.name: Nun
steps.text: Let me confirm: You're not sure if the individual currently under care will die, but you want to make funeral preparations for her?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Yes... she is not in good shape. I will do all that I can as her Nurturer.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: But that will not preclude me from preparing for the worst.

steps.name: Nun
steps.text: This seems so... un-Lateran.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: What should a Lateran be like?

steps.name: Nun
steps.text: Now that's a complicated question...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Farewell—I hope we will not have cause to meet again.
I didn't believe it when they said it—But you really did come back here, Andoain.
This Ecclesia Requietum, this field of irises... are they familiar to you? Do you reminisce over them?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: There are many Ecclesiae Requietorum in Laterano.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: As for reminiscing... it would be inappropriate for me to do that about an Ecclesia Requietum, in my present position.
I forgot. You're a high-and-mighty Nurturer now.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Who are you?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Was it you who followed me and attacked me in the shrine?
Followed? Attacked? Who's the one who's mad here, Andoain, you or me?
If you didn't want us to walk the same path as you, why did you call us 'Pathfinders'?
The sinister shrine that devours. Is it the righteous path that you've found, or one that has led you astray?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I do not recall promising to walk the same path as anyone, before I met the Matriarch...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: As for the Shrine of Nurtury, it's true that it has guided my path. But sinister? There must be some misunderstanding...
Enough, Andoain! Nugas garris! Don't play the fool with me!

spans.text: Don't play the fool with me!

steps.text: A dozen of us never came back from the shrine! If the path you found demands our sacrifice, we at least deserve to be told.
Or, if you're really shameless enough to deny the connection, at least have the decency to say it to my face!

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: No, I don't understand...
You'll have plenty of time to figure it out.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Please, don't... there are many children I must care for... and that mother...
*cough* *cough* Argh—dammit!
It's them. Pull back!

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: If I didn't know better, I would say you were trying to hit Andoain with that one.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: He's proven hard enough to kill so far. I figured it was an acceptable risk.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: Fiammetta... Mostima...

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You've really made yourself a lot of enemies, haven't you, Andoain?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: I'll go after them while you two talk.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: There's no need.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I don't know why they're targeting me, but I can't help but feel...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: They're determined. People like that inevitably have complex pasts and simple motivations.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: How compassionate.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: How could you do what you did to your own cohort, then?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Why don't you repent before Mostima and Lemuen?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Why wouldn't you tell us what the one in the Lock and Key made you see, deep in that dungeon?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Why didn't you ever give us an answer?

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: Or, more accurately, share the question with us.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: We must each follow our own paths, Fiammetta.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Is that why you attacked Lemuen and fled, before coming back with that Matriarch, hiding in the Shrine of Nurtury under her protection like nothing ever happened? Is this your 'path'?

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: What 'salvation' did you find in the years that you went off the grid?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I never found salvation, nor do I feel like nothing ever happened.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: However, life is short, and if I do not find the answer I seek soon, my sins and your pain will become meaningless.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The day after I was released from Landen Monastery, I left Laterano, believing that I would find something.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: The next five years were like a blur. All I remember is going from one place to another, alone, in many directions without end...

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I often wonder if something has gone wrong with my memory.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: And then, I found the Matriarch.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: She was headed for the Holy City, though she had been delayed greatly by helping the wounded and needy along the way.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: She made me believe that the answer still lies in Laterano.

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: She promised me a miracle, and that thousands upon thousands more miracles will be born from us. I returned to Laterano to fulfill this promise with her.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Taceas! Just shut up! You're babbling to yourself and making zero sense.

spans.text: Just shut up! You're babbling to yourself and making zero sense.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: Listen here, Andoain.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: After I kicked you out of that gathering the other day, Patrizion spent a long time telling me how important you, that shrine of yours, and the ceremony you're holding are.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I've never seen the old man so serious. So I promised him I wouldn't pick a fight with you. Yet.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: I didn't save your life because I've forgiven you.

steps.name: Fiammetta
steps.text: You just don't deserve to die before you've truly repented for what you did and paid a proper price.

steps.name: Mostima
steps.text: The Nativity is about to start, isn't it?

steps.name: Andoain
steps.text: I'm sorry, I must go.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Good morning.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Honored kindred, returned Messengers, emissaries from all across Terra, and guests who have set foot in the Holy City for the first time through the abbeys, I greet you.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: This shrine in which we now find ourselves was not built to demonstrate Laterano's power and authority for the Summit of Nations.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: However, I am glad from the bottom of my heart that it was completed in time for all of us to gather here today.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: Every birth brings new possibilities... for the continuation of faith, for the fight against calamity. Only in this way can we shape the future.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: This is even more true for the Laterano of the future.

steps.name: Matriarch
steps.text: I bid you now, prepare, and listen to the heartbeat of new life.
